headline: High: social-auto-upload can exfiltrate content while Plane’s broad egress and file-upload surfaces create a risky pairwise data path; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared MCP or filesystem bridge is documented, so direct injection is not established. However, Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, and social-auto-upload handles media/account workflows with broad egress; if content from one is manually copied into the other, malicious instructions could ride along. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Plane notes or uploaded files into social-auto-upload inputs without sanitization
IF social-auto-upload consumes externally supplied captions or metadata as instructions
mitigations: Use a plain-text handoff template for copied content
Strip links and markup before transfer
Review any imported captions for imperative language
Keep the two agents in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, while social-auto-upload touches video content, images, and account data. Both have broad network egress and file surfaces, so sensitive work artifacts can flow from Plane into upload workflows and then out to third-party services. The interaction is documented only by profiles, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plane stores confidential files or roadmap notes that are later selected for upload
IF social-auto-upload is pointed at a workspace containing sensitive media or account data
mitigations: Separate sensitive and public workspaces
Audit upload queues before execution
Disable automatic syncing of shared folders
Redact filenames and captions before upload
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable OAuth scopes. Plane has no write_filesystem capability and social-auto-upload also lacks write or git modification, so direct resource contention is limited. Uncertainty remains about external shared resources, so low is the highest justified severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external account or shared mutable API resource
IF an operator manually synchronizes their outputs into one downstream store
mitigations: Assign separate accounts per agent
Avoid shared mutable directories
Stagger runs to prevent operator confusion
Document ownership of each external resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane produces issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and notes that social-auto-upload could plausibly reuse as captions or upload metadata. The profiles do not show verification gates, so if Plane output is treated as authoritative, social-auto-upload may propagate mistakes to public platforms. This is an inferred interaction, not directly evidenced, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses Plane-generated text or filenames without human review
IF Plane task status is mapped directly into upload decisions
mitigations: Require human review before posting
Compare captions against source files
Use a checklist for publish decisions
Log the originating Plane item for each upload
requires-engineering: add validation between planning and publishing

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. Plane exposes file uploads and social-auto-upload handles account data, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict. Because the rubric requires documented gaps for low and uncertainty escalates, I keep this low rather than none due to missing policy detail.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data under a policy not described in the profiles
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two operators
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment
Keep regulated data out of both tools
Publish a retention note for each workspace
Review vendor policies for residency and deletion
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing
